subject: Television & Streaming
title: Rod Serling Before the Twilight Zone
description: A 60-second lesson on Rod Serling Before the Twilight Zone.

hook.text: Rod Serling was the angriest writer in television. Every script he wrote was a fight with network censors.

buildup.text: He wanted to write about racism, war, and injustice. Sponsors forced him to soften every story.

discovery.text: Serling realized that if he set stories on alien planets, censors wouldn't notice the social commentary.

twist.text: Science fiction became his Trojan horse. He could critique America by pretending to talk about Mars.

climax.text: This insight led him to create The Twilight Zone—a show that smuggled truth inside fantasy.

punchline.text: He hid the truth in fiction so nobody could stop him.

quiz.question: How did Rod Serling bypass network censorship?
options: He moved to a different network
He disguised social commentary as science fiction
